outcomes: Taps every square a bishop can reach, including captures and blocked diagonals
Says why a bishop can never reach a square of the other colour or a square straight ahead
Frees a boxed-in bishop with a pawn move
sources: Rewritten short on 8 Nov 2026 to the S0 standard (docs/lesson-depth-standard.md section 3); wording original.

Bishop movement is a rule of the game; the destination sets are checked by legal_destinations claims [V]. That all of those squares are one colour is arithmetic on file and rank (a1 is dark), not a machine claim [I].
Cut from the earlier long version: written move notation, bishop versus knight, attack and guard, bishop check; their items stay in content/items for Practice.

steps.text: That was a **bishop**. It slides along a **diagonal**, a line of squares that touch at their corners, any distance, and like the rook it cannot jump over pieces. From d4 it has four diagonals and 13 squares.

steps.caption: All 13 squares, along four diagonals. Straight ahead and sideways are never allowed.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the bishop on d4 can move to.

steps.caption: Own pawn on b2: the bishop stops on c3. Black pawn on f6: it may land there and capture, but not go beyond. Your own pawns can box a bishop in; moving one opens its diagonal.

claims.statement: With a white pawn on b2 and a black pawn on f6, the bishop reaches these squares and no others.

steps.caption: Moving one square sideways, or straight up or down, changes a square's colour. A diagonal step is one of each, so the colour comes back: it never changes. All seven squares marked for the c1 bishop are dark, and all seven for the f1 bishop are light. So the two bishops of one side cover both colours between them.

claims.statement: The bishop on c1 reaches exactly these squares.
The bishop on f1 reaches exactly these squares.

steps.prompt: Say it back: how does a bishop move, and why can the bishop that starts on c1 never visit a light square?

steps.text: **Compare.** A bishop slides along diagonals and stops before its own pieces or on an enemy piece it captures. A diagonal step is a sideways step plus an up-or-down step, which flip the colour twice, so the colour of its square never changes: the c1 bishop stays on dark squares for the whole game.
